ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows two concentric circles with the same center D. The ray DC goes horizontally right from D to point C on the larger circle, and the ray DA goes up-left from D to point A on the larger circle. The shaded region consists of the annular sector between rays DA and DC, together with the complementary sector of the smaller circle outside the smaller angle ADC. Reasoning: Let θ be the smaller measure of angle ADC. The radii are 1 and 2, so the area of the larger circle is 4π, the area of the smaller circle is π, and the annulus area is 4π - π = 3π. The shaded annular sector has area (θ/360)(3π). The shaded part of the smaller circle is the complementary sector, so its area is ((360 - θ)/360)(π). The total shaded area is given as (5/12)(4π) = 5π/3. Thus, (θ/360)(3π) + ((360 - θ)/360)(π) = 5π/3. Divide by π: 3θ/360 + (360 - θ)/360 = 5/3. So (2θ + 360)/360 = 5/3. Then 2θ + 360 = 600, so 2θ = 240 and θ = 120.
